title: The Forgotten Spire Revisited
premise: Zephyrine Thornbury keeps the ledgers of the Gilded Meridian, a guild that trades in impossible things, and guards the Forgotten Spire, a gate that must never open. When a century-old book of prophecies names tonight's date, Zephyrine is pulled through the gate into the dying kingdom beyond, where a thing wearing the king's crown feeds on dragon-fire to keep itself alive. Guided by a disgraced prophecy-scribe and the last dragon, Zephyrine must choose between the guild that raised him and the truth the ledgers were written to bury: the gate exists to keep the crown-thing fed, not imprisoned. He unbinds the true king, lets the last dragon-fire gutters out on his own terms, and returns through the closing gate — keeper no longer, but free.
about_author: Mirabel Thornbury is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing guild ledgers and trade manifests before turning to fantasy. She writes about people who keep records of things that should never have been recorded.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Tonight
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. While balancing the Gilded Meridian's impossible accounts, Zephyrine finds a prophecy written a century ago naming tonight's date — and his own name beneath it. The Spire's gate hums awake and pulls him through before he can burn the page. Emotional beat: dread curdling into reluctant curiosity as the keeper becomes the kept.

chapters.title: The Crown That Eats
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Beyond the gate, he witnesses the crown-thing draining dragon-fire from the last dragon while the hollowed king watches, powerless. A disgraced prophecy-scribe, Odile, reveals the guild built the gate to feed the thing, not cage it. Emotional beat: loyalty to the guild fractures as the ledgers' true purpose surfaces.

chapters.title: What the Fire Was Owed
chapters.summary: Zephyrine and Odile infiltrate the crown's ritual to unbind the king, but the guild's enforcers arrive through the gate to stop them — Zephyrine must face his own mentors. The dragon offers its final flame at a terrible price. Emotional beat: climax of sacrifice, where belonging and truth can no longer both be kept.

chapters.title: A Gate Left Open
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. The king, unbound, chooses exile over the crown; the last dragon-fire gutters out willingly, and the crown-thing starves into ash. Zephyrine returns through a gate that no longer needs a keeper, carrying the true ledgers. Emotional beat: quiet resolution — the price of survival paid, belonging redefined, truth finally recorded.
